title: AuraFlow
subtitle: Android short-form media blocker
summary: Blocks Reels, Shorts and Spotlight feeds on-device while leaving DMs and the rest of each app fully usable.
problem: Short-form video feeds are built into apps people still need for messaging. Uninstalling the app or using blunt screen-time limits removes the useful parts along with the distracting ones.
solution: AuraFlow uses Android's Accessibility Service to detect when the user enters a short-form feed inside a supported app and redirects them away, without touching chats, profiles or other screens.

architecture.detail: AccessibilityEvent stream (window state + content changes)
Per-app rule set matching view IDs and node hierarchy
Global back action / redirect away from the feed
Per-app toggles persisted locally; no network calls

features: Per-app toggles for Instagram, YouTube, Snapchat and more
Feed detection through the accessibility view hierarchy
Messaging and non-feed screens stay fully usable
On-device only: no accounts, analytics or network
reflections: Working with the Accessibility Service meant designing around UI structures I don't control. When a platform ships an update, detection can break, so the rules need to be isolated, easy to update and tested against real view dumps. It also raised a responsibility question: an app with accessibility permissions must be transparent about what it reads and must never collect it.

title: SomeFolio
subtitle: Media & download hub · Thingsbook-style tracker
summary: Offline-first tracker for anime, manga, games, film and books with live search, ratings, notes and a "what's next?" spinner.
problem: Tracking what you watch, read and play usually means a different site for every medium, each with its own account, and none of them work offline.
solution: One library for every medium, backed by free public APIs (AniList, Open Library, TVmaze, Wikipedia), stored locally by default, with optional Firestore sync that merges edits per title.

architecture.detail: React 19 + Tailwind, mobile-first, installable PWA
AniList / Open Library / TVmaze / Wikipedia search, no API keys
Local-first library with JSON export / import
Optional Firestore, per-title last-write-wins merge

features: Live cross-medium search with no API keys
Franchise stacking groups split series into one hub card
Half-star ratings, vibe tags, auto-saving notes
Workbox service worker for full offline use
reflections: Designing offline-first changed how I handled data: every edit had to be safe to make locally and merge later, which led to per-title last-write-wins sync instead of whole-library overwrites.

title: Planner & Scheduler
subtitle: Productivity dashboard with Canvas automation
summary: Task prioritization, focus timer, calendar sync and automated Canvas course-file downloads in one dashboard.
problem: Coursework is spread across Canvas, calendars and to-do lists, so planning a week means checking several tools and manually downloading course files.
solution: A single dashboard that ranks tasks by priority and due date, syncs with the calendar, runs focus sessions and pulls new Canvas files automatically.

architecture.detail: React dashboard: task board, timer, calendar view
Python service ranking tasks by urgency and importance
Canvas API poller that downloads and files new course content
Calendar integration for deadlines and study blocks

features: Priority ranking by urgency and importance
Automated Canvas file download and organization
reflections: Building a tool for my own workflow made scope creep easy. Keeping a short list of must-haves and treating everything else as a later iteration kept the project shippable.

title: Automation Extension
subtitle: Chrome workflow automation
summary: Manifest V3 extension that automates repetitive web actions: form filling, navigation sequences, page clean-up.
problem: Many everyday web tasks repeat the same clicks and inputs, which wastes time and invites mistakes.
solution: A Manifest V3 extension with content scripts that perform configured actions on matching pages, triggered from the popup or automatically.

architecture.detail: One-click triggers and per-site configuration
MV3 service worker routing messages between contexts
Content scripts scoped to matching URLs execute actions
Settings persisted with chrome.storage

features: Content scripts scoped to matching URLs
reflections: Working within Manifest V3's permission and service-worker model taught me to request only the permissions an action needs and to design around short-lived background contexts.

title: Media Downloader & Converter
subtitle: Desktop utility
summary: Script and desktop app for downloading online media and batch-converting between formats.
problem: Downloading media and converting it usually means juggling several single-purpose tools and repeating the same steps for every file.
solution: One app that queues downloads and conversions, applies presets and processes whole folders in a single run.

architecture.detail: Interface-agnostic download + conversion pipeline
Job queue with progress reporting
Reusable output profiles for audio / video / image
CLI entry point and desktop GUI on the same core

features: Batch conversion across audio, video and image formats
reflections: Separating the core logic from the interface early let the same code power both the CLI and the GUI, and made each part easier to test.

title: Aura and Artifacts
subtitle: Minecraft gameplay mod
summary: Ability skill tree, artifact weapons, custom player animations and modpack integrations.
problem: Vanilla progression is mostly gear-based, which leaves little room for character builds or distinct playstyles.
solution: An Aura skill tree that unlocks abilities as players progress, paired with artifact weapons whose effects scale with the abilities a player has chosen.

architecture.detail: Aura skill tree with branching specializations
Artifact weapons whose effects scale with chosen abilities
Custom player animation layer
Balance values in config files for fast playtest loops

reflections: Modding a large codebase I didn't write meant reading a lot before writing anything. Keeping balance values in config files made playtesting iterations much faster than recompiling for every change.

title: Roblox Experience
subtitle: Multiplayer game
summary: Multiplayer Roblox game with custom mechanics, server-authoritative scripting and hand-built assets.
problem: Building a multiplayer game means keeping gameplay fair and in sync across many clients at once.
solution: Server-authoritative game logic in Lua with client scripts limited to input and presentation, plus custom-built assets and mechanics.

architecture.detail: Authoritative game state and rule enforcement
RemoteEvents validated server-side
Input capture and presentation only
Custom models, maps and mechanics

reflections: My first multiplayer project taught me the client/server split the hard way: anything trusted on the client can be exploited, so the server has to own the game state.

title: Aeris Wildfire Suppression Network
subtitle: APSC 169 · Engineering design brief
summary: Speculative design for an autonomous drone network that detects and suppresses wildfires in their earliest stage.
brief: Need: close the gap between ignition and first response in remote, high-risk terrain.
Concept: distributed drones that patrol, detect ignitions and coordinate early suppression.
Human-in-the-loop: live data relayed to responders, who keep final authority.
Evaluated against stakeholder needs, risk and sustainability, not just feasibility.
problem: Wildfires grow fastest in the window before crews and aircraft can reach them, especially in remote terrain where detection is slow.
solution: A distributed drone network that monitors high-risk areas, detects ignitions early and deploys coordinated suppression while relaying data to human responders.

architecture.detail: Patrol drones monitoring high-risk zones
Early ignition detection and localization
Swarm tasking for coordinated suppression
Data uplink to human responders and command

features: System architecture for detection, coordination and suppression
reflections: The project pushed me to justify design decisions against stakeholder needs and constraints, not just technical feasibility. Working as a team on a speculative system also showed how much a shared problem definition matters before anyone starts designing.

title: Engineering ePortfolio
subtitle: This site
summary: Data-driven hub for engineering reflections, project reports and documentation, switchable between personal and university views.
problem: Academic work, reflections and personal projects usually end up scattered across course platforms, drives and repositories.
solution: One data-driven site where every project lives in a JSON file and can be viewed as either a personal portfolio or a university ePortfolio.

architecture.detail: projects.json + profile.json as the single source of truth
Bento grid filtered by Personal / University mode
Spec-sheet drawer: problem, solution, architecture, reflection
Vite build pushed to GitHub Pages

features: All content in two JSON files
reflections: Treating the portfolio as a product rather than a document made me think about the reader: what a recruiter and an instructor each need to find, and how quickly.
